text:
Morgan: Heads-up — our canary percentages have been oscillating when traffic bursts hit the staging pool. I prototyped a PID-style smoother on the traffic weight allocator + a lease refresh tweak to reduce fallback churn. Wanted to share the idea and get tradeoff thoughts.

Ada: can you summarize the failure modes you're seeing? oscillation = traffic swings back to baseline and then huge fallback spikes? is this client-side or router-side? @morgan

Morgan: Root cause: short-lived burst + delayed observer signal -> allocator overshoots the canary to absorb, observers then see higher latency (from cold kv-cache) and trigger fallback -> allocator reacts by cutting weight -> repeat. Mix of router-side and observer latency signal timing.

Ralph: hmm, so it's basically a feedback loop with non-negligible delay. PID makes sense conceptually, but P alone will oscillate. What about leaning on integral term carefully & adding rate limit on step changes?

Morgan: exactly. My prototype uses a PD baseline for responsiveness and a small I-term to correct steady-state bias. Also added a per-tenant max step delta (rate cap) and a cooldown window for auto-fallback to ignore transient tail blips.

Kim: how do we avoid masking real regressions? if we smooth too hard we could take too long to rollback a bad model.

Morgan: tradeoff: smoothing + hysteresis increases time-to-fallback for real regressions. To mitigate we keep a separate "safety funnel" that watches crisp regression signals (error-rate, confidence-drop, safety-checks) that bypass smoothing and trigger immediate fallback. So heuristics: latency signals go through PID smoother; correctness/safety signals short-circuit.

Ada: nice. Can you paste the rollout config you envisioned? even pseudo YAML is fine.

Morgan: pasted prototype in thread below:

```yaml
rollout_policy:
  type: canary
  step_window_seconds: 60  # observer aggregation window
  smoothing:
    controller: pid
    pid_params: {p: 0.8, i: 0.05, d: 0.2}
    max_step_pct: 10  # percent points per minute
  cooldown_seconds: 120
  safety_funnel:
    bypass_signals: ["error_rate>0.5%","safety_match>0.1%"]
  lease:
    kind: epoch
    epoch_seconds: 30  # how long a canary lease lasts before router refresh
    stale_grace_seconds: 10
```

Ralph: two quick comments: 1) pid params look aggressive for p; may still overshoot on spiky traffic. 2) epoch vs per-request lease: epoch seems good, but if epoch_seconds is too long we see stale affinity. What if we do adaptive epoch based on traffic variance?

Morgan: good points. I experimented with adaptive epoch: epoch = clamp(base * sqrt(1 + variance_score), min, max). Works better in sim. Also a fallback guard that ensures we never reduce canary by >X% in Y seconds.

dev-bot: [deploy-check] rollout_policy schema validated, no blocking issues found. :white_check_mark:

Kim: what about observability changes? we'll need per-tenant smoothing state, the pid state, and clear signals for WHEN short-circuit happened vs regular fallback. Otherwise debugging is painful.

Morgan: agreed — plan is: expose these metrics per-route & per-tenant: pid_{p,i,d}, pid_output, smoothing_step, safety_bypass_count, lease_expiry, fallback_reason. Timeline: dashboard + alert rules in 2 sprints.

Ada: ops question — oncall playbook updates? if the smoother hides an ongoing regression we want manual stop. @sheriff fyi

sheriff: yep, we need a quick kill-switch that OOs can trigger (UI + CLI). Also add an alert when smoothing output stays positive/negative beyond N minutes and safety bypasses have fired — that's a signal to escalate.

Ralph: experiment plan idea: A/B the smoother in a shadow mode first — allocator emits both smoothed and raw weights, router uses raw normally but we log what would have happened. Run for a week and compare fallback counts & mean time to detect regressions.

Morgan: love that. will add shadow mode and a canary experiment. Also will run sim with synthetic burst patterns + real trace replays.

Kim: one last: do we need any change to client SDKs or is this entirely server-side?

Morgan: server-side only for now. If we later add client-side smart routing (edge ab), we can share the allocation decisions through a small signed token. Not in scope for MVP.

Ada: cool — thanks Morgan. next steps: add experiment config, populate observability metrics, and draft oncall runbook changes. I'll pair on the dashboard tickets. :thumbsup:

Morgan: thanks all — will open PR with config + sim results tomorrow.
